steps.description: Choose Receive when money is coming in from a customer. Choose Pay when you are paying a supplier.
steps.label: Payment Type
steps.title: Money in or money out?

steps.description: Set this to Customer when receiving money, or Supplier when paying one.
steps.label: Party Type
steps.title: Customer or supplier

steps.description: Pick the customer who paid you. Their outstanding invoices load underneath once selected.
steps.label: Party
steps.title: Who paid you

steps.description: Set this to the day the money actually arrived, not today's date. When a customer pays in instalments, each payment gets its own entry with its own date, which is what builds the payment history.
steps.label: Posting Date
steps.title: The date the money arrived

steps.description: Cash, bank transfer, card and so on. Choosing this fills in the accounting side for you, so you do not have to pick accounts by hand.
steps.label: Mode of Payment
steps.title: How they paid

steps.description: Enter what was actually handed over. For a part payment, enter only that instalment, not the invoice total. Paying 5,000 against a 10,000 invoice is normal and expected.
steps.label: Paid Amount
steps.title: How much you received

steps.description: This table links the payment to the invoice it settles. Set Allocated to the part of this payment going to that invoice. The invoice then shows as Partly Paid and its outstanding balance drops by that amount.
steps.label: Payment References
steps.title: Which invoice this pays

steps.description: Money received but not matched to any invoice. Normally this should be zero. If a number appears here, an invoice line is missing or an allocated amount is too low.
steps.label: Unallocated Amount
steps.title: Check this is zero
